question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own this private host recovery protocol and restored-startup admission gate, or should the pending RFC define a smaller core seam while host lifecycle and readiness orchestration remain outside core?
rationale: The diff intentionally establishes a new recovery ownership boundary across backup state, persistent receipt records, and Gateway readiness; code review cannot determine the desired long-term product boundary from tests alone.

options.title: Accept the core recovery boundary
options.body: Approve the RFC ownership split, land the lower recovery-point and final-capture contracts first, then review this slice as their private Gateway integration.

options.title: Narrow the core seam
options.body: Keep SQLite snapshot verification and restore primitives in core but move host lifecycle identity, readiness orchestration, and admission policy behind a future adopter-owned integration.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer all three slices until a maintainer-owned recovery and scale-from-zero design specifies the supported deployment contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the core recovery boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the RFC ownership split, land the lower recovery-point and final-capture contracts first, then review this slice as their private Gateway integration.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked recovery stack and can clarify the intended contract while the repository owner decides product direction.
